title: Climbing the Ladder of Abstraction: Amelia Wattenberger
talk_summary: A design talk arguing that augmentation is really stacked small automations, and that AI can generate multiple 'zoom levels' of abstraction over information so users can act at whichever level fits the task. It is a UX/product vision (Adept) with demos of summarizing books and Airbnb listings, not an engineering talk about agent systems.

takeaways.technique: Multi-level summaries of long artifacts (zoom-out ladder)
takeaways.what_they_do: Use an LLM to progressively summarize text at several granularities (paragraph -> 10-paragraph -> chapter), keeping a minimap so you can move between levels and edit at the coarse level.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can use AI to generate these different levels, glue them together, and make it easy to move between them

takeaways.technique: Task-specific abstraction of a document before judging
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of reading the whole listing, they extract only the deciding factors (walk time, Wi-Fi sentiment from reviews, one relevant photo) into a compact view for the decision.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can use AI to pull out the relevant reviews and summarize them as positive or negative

takeaways.technique: Act at every abstraction level, not just view
takeaways.what_they_do: Each zoom level preserves the ability to take action (book, message host) so users never have to drop back to the raw source to act.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at this higher zoom level, preserving the ability to act on this information
